findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check_page_tags, product_page_seo, ai_readiness_check, landing_page_check, exposure_check, get_feedback_reply · Private data: check_ai_crawler_access, check_page_tags, trace_redirects, product_page_seo, ai_readiness_check, link_sample_check, landing_page_check, exposure_check · Public sink: check_page_tags, exposure_check, submit_feedback · Destructive: product_page_seo, ai_readiness_check, landing_page_check, submit_feedback.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check_page_tags, product_page_seo, ai_readiness_check, landing_page_check, exposure_check, get_feedback_reply · Private data: check_ai_crawler_access, check_page_tags, trace_redirects, product_page_seo, ai_readiness_check, link_sample_check, landing_page_check, exposure_check · Public sink: check_page_tags, exposure_check, submit_feedback · Destructive: product_page_seo, ai_readiness_check, landing_page_check, submit_feedback

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "check_ai_crawler_access" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
